```{r,include=F}
gg_qqplot <- function(ps, ci = 0.95, title = "QQ Plot") {
  n <- length(ps)
  df <- data.frame(
    observed = pmin(-log10(sort(ps)), 4), # Cap observed values at 4
    expected = -log10(ppoints(n)),
    clower = pmin(-log10(qbeta(p = (1 - ci) / 2, shape1 = 1:n, shape2 = n:1)), 4), # Cap clower values at 4
    cupper = pmin(-log10(qbeta(p = (1 + ci) / 2, shape1 = 1:n, shape2 = n:1)), 4)  # Cap cupper values at 4
  )

  log10Pe <- expression(paste("Expected -log"[10], plain(P)))
  log10Po <- expression(paste("Observed -log"[10], plain(P)))

  ggplot(df) +
    geom_ribbon(mapping = aes(x = expected, ymin = clower, ymax = cupper), alpha = 0.1) +
    geom_point(aes(expected, observed), size = 1.5, color = "red") +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
    xlab(log10Pe) + 
    ylab(log10Po) +
    ylim(0, 4) + # Limit y-axis to 0-5
    ggtitle(title) # Add title
}

setwd("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started")

if (author_threshold) {
  #directories <- "data/STINGseq-v1_GDO"

  grna_target_data_frame <- data.frame(read_csv(paste0(directories,"/grna_target_data_frame.csv")))
  grna_target_data_frame_omit  <- grna_target_data_frame %>%
    filter(!(grna_id %in% c("NTC-3", "NTC-12")))

  sceptre_object <- import_data_from_cellranger(
    directories = directories,
    moi = "high",
    grna_target_data_frame = grna_target_data_frame_omit
  )

  positive_control_pairs <- construct_positive_control_pairs(sceptre_object)

  discovery_pairs_cis <- construct_cis_pairs(
    sceptre_object = sceptre_object,
    positive_control_pairs = positive_control_pairs,
    response_position_data_frame=gene_position_data_frame_grch37,
    distance_threshold = 5e5
  )

  discovery_pairs_trans <- construct_trans_pairs(
    sceptre_object = sceptre_object,
    positive_control_pairs = positive_control_pairs,
    pairs_to_exclude = "pairs_containing_pc_targets"
  )

  sceptre_object <- sceptre_object |>  # |> is R's base pipe, similar to %>%
    set_analysis_parameters(
      discovery_pairs = discovery_pairs_trans,
      positive_control_pairs = positive_control_pairs,
      side = "both",
      grna_integration_strategy="singleton"
    ) |>
    assign_grnas(
      method = "thresholding",
      threshold = 1
    )

}
```

We tried different settings: 1. Data containing whole gene or subset
data containing gene of interest 2. Whether or not to normalize the gene
expression using cell library size 3. Whether or not to rank the gene
expression 4. Whether or not to use approximation to obtain p value

Data setting: The whole data containing all the gene, the propensity in
estimated using logistics regression considering the cell specific
information. (library size, etc.)

# Our model：use power sum to combine gene-wise test statistics

Besides using power sum to combine gene-wise test statistics, I also
consider the maximum test statistics as one of the combinations.

The dataset we are using now is a

1.  A subset of genes, consider only genes contained in the gene module

2.  Filtered (removing analyzing genes that have low expression among
    all cells)

3.  Normalized (divide expression by the library size)

4.  Ranked (ranking the gene-expression level)

5.  Filtered (removing cells that have low library size \<1300 total UMI
    counts)

## Consider perturbations that affects >150 cells

```{r}
infect_cell_threshold <- 150

gene_modules <- readRDS("data/gene_modules_id.rds")

gene_wise_p  <- read.csv("output/newest/pooled_variance_median/gene_wise_p.csv", nrows = 207)[rowSums(get_grna_assignments(
  sceptre_object = sceptre_object
)[-208,])>infect_cell_threshold,]


gene_wise_p[gene_wise_p == 0] <- 1 / 10000
gene_wise_p[gene_wise_p >= 1] <- 1- 1/10000
sceptre <- rbind(readRDS("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/output/both_trans_author_filtered_cell_complete/results_run_discovery_analysis.rds")[,c(1,2,7)],
                 readRDS("/project/xuanyao/jiaming/Getting_started/output/both_trans_author_filtered_cell_complete/results_run_calibration_check.rds")[,c(1,2,7)])

sceptre <- sceptre[!is.na(sceptre$p_value), ]
sceptre$p_value[sceptre$p_value == 1] <- 1 - 1e-6

sceptre_wide <- sceptre %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = response_id, values_from = p_value) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Set the row names to be the grna_id and remove the grna_id column
rownames(sceptre_wide) <- sceptre_wide$grna_id
sceptre_wide <- sceptre_wide[, -1]

sceptre_wide <- sceptre_wide[rownames(gene_wise_p)[rownames(gene_wise_p) %in% rownames(sceptre_wide)], ]

sceptre_wide <- sceptre_wide[, colnames(gene_wise_p), drop = FALSE]



library(ACAT)
module_results <- list()

# Iterate over each row of t_gene_p_no_approximation to compute ACAT p-values for each module
for (i in seq_len(nrow(gene_wise_p))) {
  grna_id <- rownames(gene_wise_p)[i]
  p_values_row <- gene_wise_p[i,] 
  
  # Initialize an empty list to store ACAT p-values and module names for each module
  module_acat_pvals <- c()
  module_names <- c()
  
  # Iterate over each module in gene_modules to combine p-values using ACAT
  for (j in seq_along(gene_modules)) {
    module_name <- names(gene_modules)[j]  # Get the module name
    module_genes <- gene_modules[[j]][gene_modules[[j]] %in% colnames(p_values_row)]
    
    # Only apply ACAT if there are genes to combine and they are not NA
    if (length(module_genes) > 0) {
      module_p_values <- as.numeric(p_values_row[module_genes])
      module_p_values <- module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)]  # Remove NAs
      
      # Check if module_p_values still has values after removing NAs
      if (length(module_p_values) > 0) {
        # acat_pval <- ACAT(module_p_values)
        acat_pval<-combination.test(module_p_values,weights = NA,method = "Cauchy",tail.idx = 1)
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, acat_pval)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      } else {
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      }
    } else {
      module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
      module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
    }
  }
  
  # Store results as a data frame in the list
  module_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    grna_id = grna_id,
    module = module_names,
    acat_pval = module_acat_pvals
  )
}


# Combine all results into a single data frame
module_results_t <- do.call(rbind, module_results)


module_results <- list()

# Iterate over each row of t_gene_no_approximation to compute Bonferroni p-values for each module
for (i in seq_len(nrow(gene_wise_p))) {
  grna_id <- rownames(gene_wise_p)[i]
  p_values_row <- gene_wise_p[i, ]
  
  # Initialize an empty list to store Bonferroni p-values and module names for each module
  module_acat_pvals <- c()
  module_names <- c()

  # Iterate over each module in gene_modules to combine p-values using Bonferroni
  for (j in seq_along(gene_modules)) {
    module_name <- names(gene_modules)[j]  # Get the module name
    module_genes <- gene_modules[[j]][gene_modules[[j]] %in% colnames(p_values_row)]
    
    # Only apply Bonferroni if there are genes to combine and they are not NA
    if (length(module_genes) > 0) {
      module_p_values <- as.numeric(p_values_row[module_genes])
      module_p_values <- module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)]  # Remove NAs
      
      # Check if module_p_values still has values after removing NAs
      if (length(module_p_values) > 0) {
        # Bonferroni adjustment: multiply smallest p-value by number of tests
        bonferroni_pval <- min(module_p_values) * length(module_p_values)
        bonferroni_pval <- min(bonferroni_pval, 1)  # Cap p-values at 1
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, bonferroni_pval)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      } else {
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      }
    } else {
      module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
      module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
    }
  }

  # Store results as a data frame in the list
  module_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    grna_id = grna_id,
    module = module_names,
    bonferroni_pval = module_acat_pvals
  )
}

# Combine all results into a single data frame
```

```{r,fig.width=8,fig.height=8,warning=F}
plot_list <- list()

# Loop through significant levels and display plots
for (significant_level in significant_levels) {
  # Filter significant IDs for each method
  significant_ids_gene_wise_p <- module_results_sceptre$identifier[
    module_results_sceptre$bh_pval < significant_level]
  
    significant_ids_gene_wise_p_bonfer <- module_results_sceptre_bonforroni$identifier[
    module_results_sceptre_bonforroni$bh_pval < significant_level]
    
    
  significant_ids_gene_wise_p_t <- module_results_t$identifier[
    module_results_t$bh_pval < significant_level]
  
    significant_ids_gene_wise_p_t_bonfer <- module_results_t_bonforroni$identifier[
    module_results_t_bonforroni$bh_pval < significant_level]
  
 significant_ids_minp <- minp_long$identifier[
    minp_long$bh_pval < significant_level]
  
  significant_ids_ours <- our_method_long$identifier[
    our_method_long$bh_pval < significant_level]
  
  # Prepare the sets
  venn_data <- list(
    `Sceptre+Cauchy` = significant_ids_gene_wise_p,
    `t+Cauchy` = significant_ids_gene_wise_p_t,
    `minp` = significant_ids_minp,
    `Our method` = significant_ids_ours
    # `Sceptre+Bonfer` = significant_ids_gene_wise_p_bonfer,
    # `t+Bonfer`=significant_ids_gene_wise_p_t_bonfer
  )
  
  # Generate the Euler diagram and display it
  euler_plot <- plot(euler(venn_data),
                     fills = list(fill = c("red", "purple", "green", "yellow","purple"), alpha = 0.5),
                     edges = TRUE, quantities = TRUE,
                     main = paste("Significant level", significant_level)
  )
  
  
  
plot_list[[length(plot_list) + 1]] <- euler_plot
}
```

```{r,echo=F,fig.width=8, fig.height=8}
library(eulerr)


module_results <- list()

# Iterate over each row of t_gene_p_no_approximation to compute ACAT p-values for each module
for (i in seq_len(nrow(gene_wise_p))) {
  grna_id <- rownames(gene_wise_p)[i]
  p_values_row <- gene_wise_p[i,] 
  
  # Initialize an empty list to store ACAT p-values and module names for each module
  module_acat_pvals <- c()
  module_names <- c()
  
  # Iterate over each module in gene_modules to combine p-values using ACAT
  for (j in seq_along(gene_modules)) {
    module_name <- names(gene_modules)[j]  # Get the module name
    module_genes <- gene_modules[[j]][gene_modules[[j]] %in% colnames(p_values_row)]
    
    # Only apply ACAT if there are genes to combine and they are not NA
    if (length(module_genes) > 0) {
      module_p_values <- as.numeric(p_values_row[module_genes])
      module_p_values <- module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)]  # Remove NAs
      
      # Check if module_p_values still has values after removing NAs
      if (length(module_p_values) > 0) {
        # acat_pval <- ACAT(module_p_values)
        acat_pval<-combination.test(module_p_values,weights = NA,method = "Cauchy",tail.idx = 1)
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, acat_pval)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      } else {
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      }
    } else {
      module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
      module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
    }
  }
  
  # Store results as a data frame in the list
  module_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    grna_id = grna_id,
    module = module_names,
    acat_pval = module_acat_pvals
  )
}

module_results <- list()

# Iterate over each row of t_gene_no_approximation to compute Bonferroni p-values for each module
for (i in seq_len(nrow(gene_wise_p))) {
  grna_id <- rownames(gene_wise_p)[i]
  p_values_row <- gene_wise_p[i, ]
  
  # Initialize an empty list to store Bonferroni p-values and module names for each module
  module_acat_pvals <- c()
  module_names <- c()

  # Iterate over each module in gene_modules to combine p-values using Bonferroni
  for (j in seq_along(gene_modules)) {
    module_name <- names(gene_modules)[j]  # Get the module name
    module_genes <- gene_modules[[j]][gene_modules[[j]] %in% colnames(p_values_row)]
    
    # Only apply Bonferroni if there are genes to combine and they are not NA
    if (length(module_genes) > 0) {
      module_p_values <- as.numeric(p_values_row[module_genes])
      module_p_values <- module_p_values[!is.na(module_p_values)]  # Remove NAs
      
      # Check if module_p_values still has values after removing NAs
      if (length(module_p_values) > 0) {
        # Bonferroni adjustment: multiply smallest p-value by number of tests
        bonferroni_pval <- min(module_p_values) * length(module_p_values)
        bonferroni_pval <- min(bonferroni_pval, 1)  # Cap p-values at 1
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, bonferroni_pval)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      } else {
        module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
        module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
      }
    } else {
      module_acat_pvals <- c(module_acat_pvals, NA)
      module_names <- c(module_names, module_name)
    }
  }

  # Store results as a data frame in the list
  module_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    grna_id = grna_id,
    module = module_names,
    bonferroni_pval = module_acat_pvals
  )
}
```

```{r}
gg_qqplot_two <- function(ps1, ps2, ci = 0.95, title = "QQ Plot", labels = c("Dataset 1", "Dataset 2")) {
  n <- length(ps1)
  df1 <- data.frame(
    observed = pmin(-log10(sort(ps1)), 4), # Cap observed values at 4
    expected = -log10(ppoints(n)),
    dataset = labels[1]
  )
  
  n2 <- length(ps2)
  df2 <- data.frame(
    observed = pmin(-log10(sort(ps2)), 4), # Cap observed values at 4
    expected = -log10(ppoints(n2)),
    dataset = labels[2]
  )
  
  # Combine datasets
  df <- rbind(df1, df2)
  
  # Compute confidence intervals
  clower <- pmin(-log10(qbeta(p = (1 - ci) / 2, shape1 = 1:n, shape2 = n:1)), 4)
  cupper <- pmin(-log10(qbeta(p = (1 + ci) / 2, shape1 = 1:n, shape2 = n:1)), 4)
  ci_df <- data.frame(expected = -log10(ppoints(n)), clower = clower, cupper = cupper)

  log10Pe <- expression(paste("Expected -log"[10], plain(P)))
  log10Po <- expression(paste("Observed -log"[10], plain(P)))

  ggplot() +
    geom_ribbon(data = ci_df, aes(x = expected, ymin = clower, ymax = cupper), alpha = 0.4, fill = "grey") +
    geom_point(data = df, aes(x = expected, y = observed, color = dataset), size = 1.5) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
    xlab(log10Pe) +
    ylab(log10Po) +
    ylim(0, 4) + # Limit y-axis to 0-4
    ggtitle(title) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "blue")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(legend.title = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
}

gg_qqplot_two(as.vector(ntc_our$p_value), as.vector(ntc_sceptre$acat_pval), title="Negative control p values", labels = c("Our Method", "Sceptre+Cauchy"))
```

**Notes:**

*1. In the above plot, the perturbations are randomly chosen*
*2. We calculate the p values for two-sided t-test by*

$min(2 \times\frac{min(\#left,\#right)}{\#permutation},1)$

$\#left$ *means how many null test statistics are smaller than observed
test statistics.*

### Compute the glm test statistics using the glm function in R


```r
round_response<-round(response_matrix_raw[gene_idx,])
par(mfrow = c(3, 2))

grna_indices <- seq(1, by = nrow(grna_assignment_matrix), length.out = (n_permute+1))


subset_grna_assignment_matrix <- grna_assignment_matrix_combined[grna_indices, ]


for (k in 1:nrow(round_response)){
  
z_values <- vector("list", 800)

# Loop through the permutations
for (i in 1:800) {
  # Fit the GLM model
model <- glm.nb(
  round_response[k, ] ~ subset_grna_assignment_matrix[i, ] + log(covariate$response_n_umis)
)
  
    coef <- coef(summary(model))  # Summary of the model
  
  # Calculate the z-value for the predictor variable
  z_values[i] <- coef[2, "Estimate"] / coef[2, "Std. Error"]
}


hist(
  as.numeric(z_values),
  main = paste0("Test statistics of ", rownames(grna_assignment_matrix)[grna_indices[1]],"-", rownames(round_response)[k]), xlab="null test statistics", breaks=800
)

abline(v = z_values[[1]], col = "red", lwd = 2)

# Optionally, add a label for the value
text(z_values[[1]], par("usr")[4] * 0.9, "Observed", col = "red", pos = 4)

}
```

```{r}
response_matrix <- as.matrix(response_matrix)
  grna_assignment_matrix <- as.matrix(weird_assignment)

  n_cells <- ncol(response_matrix)
  n_genes <- nrow(response_matrix)
  all_cells <- seq_len(n_cells)
  n_rows <- nrow(grna_assignment_matrix)

  response_matrix_t <- t(response_matrix)
  response_matrix_t_squared <-response_matrix_t^2

  grna_infected_cell_count <- rowSums(grna_assignment_matrix)

  mean_expression_trt <- grna_assignment_matrix %*% response_matrix_t / grna_infected_cell_count
  mean_expression_squared_trt <- grna_assignment_matrix %*% response_matrix_t_squared / grna_infected_cell_count
  var_expression_trt <- mean_expression_squared_trt - mean_expression_trt^2

  grna_control_cell_count <- n_cells - grna_infected_cell_count
  mean_expression_control <- (1 - grna_assignment_matrix) %*% response_matrix_t / grna_control_cell_count
  mean_expression_squared_control <- (1 - grna_assignment_matrix) %*% response_matrix_t_squared / grna_control_cell_count
  var_expression_control <- mean_expression_squared_control - mean_expression_control^2

  t_statistics <- (mean_expression_trt - mean_expression_control) / sqrt(var_expression_trt / grna_infected_cell_count + var_expression_control / grna_control_cell_count)
```

**Those spikes indicate an unstable resampled null test statistics, revealing problems in resampling. We want to check whether it is a lack of cells infected by gRNA that leads to a bad logistic regression, and therefore an unstable resample**


```r
n_permute <-3000
n_rows <-nrow(get_grna_assignments(
    sceptre_object = sceptre_object
  )[-208,-cell_to_filter])

chunk_size <- 15

chunks <- split(1:n_rows, rep(1:ceiling(n_rows / chunk_size), each = chunk_size, length.out = n_rows))

combined_num_spike <- NULL
combined_cell_infected <- NULL
combined_proportion <- NULL

for (rows in chunks){
  
 grna_assignment_matrix <-get_grna_assignments(
    sceptre_object = sceptre_object
  )[rows,-cell_to_filter]

source("code/functions.R")
 set.seed(0)
  grna_assignment_matrix_combined <- permutation_or_resampling(grna_assignment_matrix, n_permute, use_resample)

  test_result <- t_test(response_matrix, grna_assignment_matrix_combined)

  gene_wise_test_tensor <-  convert_matrix_to_tensor(test_result, n_permute, grna_assignment_matrix)
  
  
num_spike <- numeric(length(rows))
proportion<- numeric(length(rows))

for (i in 1:length(rows)) {
  num_spike[i] <- sum(abs(gene_wise_test_tensor[,,i]) > 30, na.rm = TRUE)
  proportion[i] <- sum(apply(abs(gene_wise_test_tensor[,,i]), 2, function(col) any(col > 30, na.rm = TRUE)))

}

cell_infected <- rowSums(grna_assignment_matrix)


  combined_num_spike <- c(combined_num_spike, num_spike)
  combined_cell_infected <- c(combined_cell_infected, cell_infected)
  combined_proportion <- c(combined_proportion,proportion)
}
```

```r
df <- data.frame(
  combined_cell_infected = combined_cell_infected,
  combined_num_spike = combined_num_spike,
  combined_proportion=combined_proportion
)

df <- df %>% arrange(combined_cell_infected)


barplot(
  height = df$combined_proportion,
  names.arg = df$combined_cell_infected,
  xlab = "Num Cell Infected",
  ylab = "Num werid spikes",
  main = "Number of genes that have weird histogram",
  col = "skyblue",
  border = "black",
  las = 2 # Rotate x-axis labels for readability
)


barplot(
  height = df$combined_num_spike,
  names.arg = df$combined_cell_infected,
  xlab = "Num Cell Infected",
  ylab = "Num werid spikes",
  main = "Sum of weird spikes in histograms among all genes",
  col = "skyblue",
  border = "black",
  las = 2 # Rotate x-axis labels for readability
)
```

session**

## Comparison of Module p values (minp vs our method)


Minp:
This gene-module p value is obtained by : 1. Obtain gene-wise test
statistics and their corresponding p value 2. Take minimum p value
within a gene module, as the test statistics 3. Use null distribution to
find final p value


**We want to investigate in which case minp has a significance
difference from us**


```{r}
assignment_to_analyze<-matrix(as.numeric(grna_assignment_matrix[40,]),nrow=1)


prop<-estimate_propensity(assignment_to_analyze, covariate)
weight<-prop


weight[assignment_to_analyze==1] <- (1/prop[assignment_to_analyze==1])/sum(1/prop[assignment_to_analyze==1])
weight[assignment_to_analyze==0] <- (1/(1-prop[assignment_to_analyze==0]))/sum(1/(1-prop[assignment_to_analyze==0]))
balanced_covariate<-covariate$response_n_umis*weight



hist(balanced_covariate[assignment_to_analyze == 1],
     breaks = length(covariate$response_n_umis[assignment_to_analyze == 1])/5,
     col = rgb(1, 0, 0), # Add transparency
     xlim = range(balanced_covariate),
     main = "Histogram of Balanced Covariate by Assignment",
     xlab = "Balanced Covariate",
     ylab = "Frequency")

     breaks = 1000,
```
